Explain in your own words what 'Epidermal Tissue System' refers to.
questions.a: The outermost protective layer of a plant, consisting of epidermal cells, stomata for gas exchange, and appendages like trichomes or root hairs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Epidermal Tissue System'.
questions.a: The epidermis acts as a barrier and regulator for water loss and gas exchange.

Explain in your own words what 'Vascular Tissue System' refers to.
questions.a: A complex conducting system in plants made up of xylem and phloem, organized into vascular bundles that may be open or closed depending on the presence of cambium.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Vascular Tissue System'.
questions.a: Cambium presence determines whether a vascular bundle can support secondary growth.

Explain in your own words what 'Dicot vs Monocot Root Anatomy' refers to.
questions.a: Root anatomy comparison focusing on the number of xylem bundles (polyarch in monocots) and the presence of secondary growth in dicots.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dicot vs Monocot Root Anatomy'.
questions.a: Monocot roots are polyarch with large pith, while dicot roots have fewer xylem bundles and undergo secondary growth.
